newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel steady despite prompt sale.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel steady despite prompt sale.

text.p: Singapore middle distillates market was steady on Friday despite an aggressive offer by one trader which drew several buyers forcing the seller to announce that he only had one cargo for sale, traders said.
The Malaysian trader sold a 150,000-barrel July 15-19 lifting cargo at $21.70 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, down 70 cents from Thursday's lowest offer.
The low offer attracted several firm buyers but the seller then backed off leaving the market to pick at the next best offer at a hefty $22.50 which did not entice anyone to buy.
Traders said apart from the one trader's aggressive offer there was no fundamental change to the market with most expecting China to return in a fairly big way to buy late July and August cargoes.
Aside from China, traders were also counting on the closed arbitrage from the West and higher demand from Indonesia and India for August cargoes to lift the market.

Taiwan state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) is expected to award a tender to sell 225,000-250,000 barrels of gas oil at below Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, a CPC source said.
Jet fuel is current assessed at about $2.50 per barrel above gas oil.

The source said the award price was at more than a 10 cent discount to spot Singapore prices on fob Kaoshiung basis for July 23-27 lifting.
CPC chose to award the contract on a floating basis as the fixed price bids were below their expectations, the source said.
In the jet fuel market, a 225,000 barrel cargo lifting July 13-17 was offered at $24.70 per barrel free-on-board (fob), almost unchanged from Thursday's $24.65 traded level.
Traders said the jet market is steady but might come under some selling pressure as refiners seek to optimise jet fuel production in the face of the wide regrade.
